newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian Congress to investigate chief prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: Colombian Congress to investigate chief prosecutor.

text.p: Colombia's Congress is preparing to open an official investigation into chief prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso's alleged use of secret U.S. funds for the payment of witnesses in drug-corruption cases, authorities said on Friday.

Judicial sources said the investigation would be carried out by the Committee of Accusations of the House of Representatives and would be based on recent charges made by Attorney General Orlando Vasquez Velasquez.

Vasquez, who was jailed on drug corruption charges Tuesday, has accused Valdivieso of using an illegal U.S. slush fund to entice witnesses into testifying against prominent government officials, including himself.

Vasquez, a former interior minister, was arrested on orders from Valdivieso on charges that he accepted thousands of dollars in payments from leading drug traffickers, both before and after he was sworn in as attorney general in 1994.
He has denied any wrongdoing, but his U.S. travel visa was revoked in April because of his alleged links to drug lords.

Guillermo Pallomari, the self-confessed Cali drug cartel treasurer who surrendered to U.S. drug agents in the United States last year, has testified that Vasquez maintained closer ties with the cartel's jailed leaders than perhaps any other politician in Colombia.

Roberto Moya, president of the Committee of Accusations, told reporters Thursday night that a special investigator would appointed by fellow committeee members next week to spearhead the probe into Valdivieso's alleged use of secret U.S. funds.

Valdivieso, who has denied any secret U.S. funding of his office, which is autonomous and operates independently of the executive branch, told reporters that he was prepared to cooperate fully with any congressional probe.
